EXP-001.title: Does buying a dip help?
EXP-001.question: Do unusually weak stocks tend to bounce?
EXP-001.test: Apply the fixed signal and trading rules to the original five large stocks.
EXP-001.result: Test-period trades roughly broke even after costs. Some stocks lost money.
EXP-001.limitation: A small, selected sample. These historical results have already been examined.

EXP-002.title: Does it work across more stocks?
EXP-002.question: Does the same signal hold up across more stocks and years?
EXP-002.test: Keep V1 unchanged and compare annual test periods with stocks and SPY.
EXP-002.result: The overall average was positive, but the required stock-breadth test failed. The 2022 trade result was negative.
EXP-002.limitation: Today's surviving stocks were used. Broad value beyond the benchmark is still unproven.
EXP-002.next: See differences across stocks and years

EXP-004.title: How should we exit a dip?
EXP-004.question: Can different exits capture more of the same rebound?
EXP-004.test: Select registered candidates using training data only, then compare yearly outcomes on the same independent entries.
EXP-004.result: Adaptive exits beat V1's historical EV, but holding ten bars averaged more. Adaptive exits allowed larger losses.
EXP-004.limitation: Many candidates and consumed history. A better prospective strategy has not been established.

EXP-003.title: Can we trust and preserve the data?
EXP-003.question: Why were stocks excluded, and how can future signals be recorded fairly?
EXP-003.test: Inspect fresh copies of rejected price histories and build a manual signal archive.
EXP-003.result: Tiny price inconsistencies were found. Data was not repaired; future performance was not tested.
EXP-003.limitation: Original rejected downloads were not saved. New copies cannot prove their exact contents.
